::: {.route-question}
Question for today: CellCo must add capacity before it knows the demand. Which option should it choose, and what does the answer depend on?
:::

## The case: CellCo adds capacity {#cellco}

::: {.case}
::: {.facts}
CellCo makes LFP battery cells for energy storage and electric vehicles. The board wants **2 GWh per year** more capacity.

Demand three years from now is uncertain: it may be low, medium or high. The board must commit before it knows which.

Each option is scored by its net present value (NPV) in CNY million over ten years.
:::
::: {.options}
::: {.opt}
**A · New LFP line.** Largest gain, largest loss.
:::
::: {.opt}
**B · Sodium-ion retrofit** of an existing line. Cheaper, less upside.
:::
::: {.opt}
**C · Tolling contract** with a partner plant. Small and safe.
:::
::: {.opt .d}
**D · Do nothing.** NPV 0 in every state.
:::
:::
:::

[CellCo and every number in this course are fictional, written for teaching.]{.source}

## Four elements of a decision {#elements}

::: {.elements}
::: {.el}
[Alternatives]{.label}
What you can choose.

[A, B, C, D]{.ex}
:::
::: {.el}
[States of nature]{.label}
What happens that you cannot control.

[Low, medium, high demand]{.ex}
:::
::: {.el}
[Payoffs]{.label}
The result of each alternative in each state.

[NPV, CNY million]{.ex}
:::
::: {.el .key}
[Criterion]{.label}
The rule that turns a table into a choice.

[Today: five rules without probabilities, then EMV and utility]{.ex}
:::
:::

::: {.bridge}
The first three come from the problem. The fourth is a choice you make, and it can change the answer.
:::

## Five criteria without probabilities {#criteria}

```{=html}
<table class="wide">
  <thead><tr><th>Criterion</th><th>Rule</th><th>Score of A, B, C, D</th><th>Choice</th><th>Attitude it encodes</th></tr></thead>
  <tbody>
    <tr><td>Maximax</td><td>Best of the best cases</td><td class="num">260, 150, 70, 0</td><td class="hit">A</td><td>Optimist</td></tr>
    <tr><td>Maximin</td><td>Best of the worst cases</td><td class="num">−120, −40, 10, 0</td><td class="hit">C</td><td>Pessimist</td></tr>
    <tr><td>Hurwicz, α = 0.6</td><td>α · best + (1 − α) · worst</td><td class="num">108, 74, 46, 0</td><td class="hit">A</td><td>Set by α</td></tr>
    <tr><td>Laplace</td><td>Average, states equally likely</td><td class="num">73.3, 56.7, 40, 0</td><td class="hit">A</td><td>No information</td></tr>
    <tr><td>Minimax regret</td><td>Smallest maximum regret</td><td class="num">130, 110, 190, 260</td><td class="hit">B</td><td>Fear of hindsight</td></tr>
  </tbody>
</table>
```

::: {.bridge}
Three criteria pick A, one picks C and one picks B. The data did not change; only the rule did.
:::

## How optimistic is the board? {#hurwicz data-hold="true"}

```{=html}
<div class="widget" id="hw">
  <div class="w-controls">
    <label class="w-slider">Optimism α <strong id="hw-a">0.60</strong>
      <input type="range" id="hw-in" min="0" max="1" step="0.01" value="0.6" aria-describedby="hw-out">
    </label>
  </div>
  <svg id="hw-svg" viewBox="0 0 1160 250" role="img" aria-label="Hurwicz score of each alternative at the chosen optimism"></svg>
  <div class="w-strip" id="hw-strip" aria-hidden="true"></div>
  <div class="w-readout" id="hw-out" aria-live="polite"></div>
</div>
<script>
(function () {
  const root = document.getElementById('hw');
  if (!root) return;
  root.addEventListener('click', (e) => e.stopPropagation());
  const O = [['A', 'New LFP line', -120, 260, '#0F6E6B'], ['B', 'Sodium-ion retrofit', -40, 150, '#E29A2D'],
             ['C', 'Tolling contract', 10, 70, '#BE654C'], ['D', 'Do nothing', 0, 0, '#5A91BE']];
  const W = 1160, L = 260, R = 30, x0 = -150, x1 = 300;
  const X = (v) => L + (v - x0) / (x1 - x0) * (W - L - R);
  const score = (o, a) => a * o[3] + (1 - a) * o[2];
  function best(a) { let b = O[0]; for (const o of O) if (score(o, a) > score(b, a) + 1e-9) b = o; return b; }
  // Strip: which alternative wins along alpha from 0 to 1
  let segs = [], prev = null, start = 0;
  for (let i = 0; i <= 1000; i++) { const a = i / 1000, b = best(a)[0]; if (b !== prev) { if (prev) segs.push([prev, start, a]); prev = b; start = a; } }
  segs.push([prev, start, 1]);
  const col = Object.fromEntries(O.map((o) => [o[0], o[4]]));
  document.getElementById('hw-strip').innerHTML = segs.map(([k, a, b]) =>
    `<span style="width:${(b - a) * 100}%;background:${col[k]}">${b - a > 0.03 ? k + (b - a > 0.15 ? ' best for α ' + a.toFixed(2) + '–' + b.toFixed(2) : '') : ''}</span>`).join('');
  function draw() {
    const a = +document.getElementById('hw-in').value;
    document.getElementById('hw-a').textContent = a.toFixed(2);
    const b = best(a);
    let g = '';
    for (const v of [-150, -100, -50, 0, 50, 100, 150, 200, 250, 300]) g += `<line x1="${X(v)}" x2="${X(v)}" y1="8" y2="214" stroke="${v === 0 ? '#333F4A' : '#B9C1C6'}" stroke-width="${v === 0 ? 1.5 : 1}"/><text x="${X(v)}" y="238" text-anchor="middle" font-size="17" fill="#333F4A">${String(v).replace('-', '−')}</text>`;
    O.forEach((o, i) => {
      const y = 14 + i * 50, s = score(o, a);
      g += `<text x="${L - 16}" y="${y + 26}" text-anchor="end" font-size="20" font-weight="${o === b ? 700 : 400}" fill="#1C242B">${o[0]} · ${o[1]}</text>`;
      g += `<rect x="${Math.min(X(0), X(s))}" y="${y + 6}" width="${Math.max(2, Math.abs(X(s) - X(0)))}" height="30" fill="${o[4]}" ${o === b ? 'stroke="#1C242B" stroke-width="2.5"' : 'opacity=".75"'}/>`;
      g += `<text x="${s >= 0 ? X(s) + 8 : X(s) - 8}" y="${y + 28}" text-anchor="${s >= 0 ? 'start' : 'end'}" font-size="18" fill="#1C242B">${s.toFixed(1).replace('-', '−')}</text>`;
    });
    document.getElementById('hw-svg').innerHTML = g;
    document.getElementById('hw-out').innerHTML = `At α = ${a.toFixed(2)} the Hurwicz criterion picks <span class="best">${b[0]} · ${b[1]}</span>. ` +
      `α = 0 is maximin, α = 1 is maximax.`;
  }
  document.getElementById('hw-in').addEventListener('input', draw);
  draw();
})();
</script>
```

## Regret: the cost of hindsight {#regret}

```{=html}
<table class="wide">
  <thead><tr><th>Regret = best in that state − this payoff</th><th class="num">Low</th><th class="num">Medium</th><th class="num">High</th><th class="num">Maximum regret</th></tr></thead>
  <tbody>
    <tr><td>Best payoff in the state</td><td class="num ref">10 (C)</td><td class="num ref">80 (A)</td><td class="num ref">260 (A)</td><td></td></tr>
    <tr><td>A · New LFP line</td><td class="num">130</td><td class="num">0</td><td class="num">0</td><td class="num">130</td></tr>
    <tr><td>B · Sodium-ion retrofit</td><td class="num">50</td><td class="num">20</td><td class="num">110</td><td class="num hit">110</td></tr>
    <tr><td>C · Tolling contract</td><td class="num">0</td><td class="num">40</td><td class="num">190</td><td class="num">190</td></tr>
    <tr><td>D · Do nothing</td><td class="num">10</td><td class="num">80</td><td class="num">260</td><td class="num">260</td></tr>
  </tbody>
</table>
```

::: {.bridge}
Minimax regret picks B: its worst regret, 110, is the smallest. B is never the best choice in any single state, yet it is never far from the best.
:::

## Activity 1 · The option nobody picks {#act1 .activity data-hold="true"}

[Pairs · 10 minutes · paper and calculator]{.act-label}

::: {.prompt}
A consultant adds option **E · Mega-line, 3 GWh**, with payoffs −200, 20 and 300. Redo the regret table with E included.
:::

1. Which option does minimax regret pick now?
2. Is E itself chosen?
3. Did adding E change the choice between A, B, C and D? Why does this matter for a board meeting?

[Hint: only one column has a new best payoff.]{.hint}

::: {.selfstudy}
Studying alone: write your three answers before you go to the next slide.
:::

## Activity 1 · Answer {#act1-answer}

```{=html}
<table class="wide">
  <thead><tr><th>Regret with E included</th><th class="num">Low</th><th class="num">Medium</th><th class="num">High</th><th class="num">Maximum regret</th></tr></thead>
  <tbody>
    <tr><td>Best payoff in the state</td><td class="num ref">10 (C)</td><td class="num ref">80 (A)</td><td class="num ref">300 (E)</td><td></td></tr>
    <tr><td>A · New LFP line</td><td class="num">130</td><td class="num">0</td><td class="num">40</td><td class="num hit">130</td></tr>
    <tr><td>B · Sodium-ion retrofit</td><td class="num">50</td><td class="num">20</td><td class="num">150</td><td class="num">150</td></tr>
    <tr><td>C · Tolling contract</td><td class="num">0</td><td class="num">40</td><td class="num">230</td><td class="num">230</td></tr>
    <tr><td>D · Do nothing</td><td class="num">10</td><td class="num">80</td><td class="num">300</td><td class="num">300</td></tr>
    <tr><td>E · Mega-line</td><td class="num">210</td><td class="num">60</td><td class="num">0</td><td class="num">210</td></tr>
  </tbody>
</table>
```

::: {.bridge}
E is not chosen, but the choice moves from B to A. Minimax regret depends on which options are on the table, so a proposal that will be rejected can still decide the outcome.
:::

## Decisions under risk: expected monetary value {#emv}

```{=html}
<div class="formula"><p>EMV(<i>a</i>) = Σ<sub><i>s</i></sub> <i>p</i><sub><i>s</i></sub> · payoff(<i>a</i>, <i>s</i>)</p></div>
```

```{=html}
<table class="wide">
  <thead><tr><th>Alternative</th><th class="num">Low, p = 0.3</th><th class="num">Medium, p = 0.5</th><th class="num">High, p = 0.2</th><th class="num">EMV</th></tr></thead>
  <tbody>
    <tr><td>A · New LFP line</td><td class="num">−120</td><td class="num">80</td><td class="num">260</td><td class="num hit">56</td></tr>
    <tr><td>B · Sodium-ion retrofit</td><td class="num">−40</td><td class="num">60</td><td class="num">150</td><td class="num">48</td></tr>
    <tr><td>C · Tolling contract</td><td class="num">10</td><td class="num">40</td><td class="num">70</td><td class="num">37</td></tr>
    <tr><td>D · Do nothing</td><td class="num">0</td><td class="num">0</td><td class="num">0</td><td class="num">0</td></tr>
  </tbody>
</table>
```

[EMV picks A at CNY 56 million. It assumes the board is risk-neutral: a loss of 120 weighs exactly as much as a gain of 120.]{.note-line}

## Expected opportunity loss {#eol}

::: {.two}
::: {}
EOL is the expected regret: weight each regret by the state probability.

EOL(A) = 0.3 × 130 + 0.5 × 0 + 0.2 × 0 = **39**

For every alternative, EMV + EOL = **95**. Minimizing EOL and maximizing EMV always give the same choice.
:::
::: {}
```{=html}
<table class="wide">
  <thead><tr><th>Alternative</th><th class="num">EMV</th><th class="num">EOL</th><th class="num">Sum</th></tr></thead>
  <tbody>
    <tr><td>A</td><td class="num hit">56</td><td class="num hit">39</td><td class="num">95</td></tr>
    <tr><td>B</td><td class="num">48</td><td class="num">47</td><td class="num">95</td></tr>
    <tr><td>C</td><td class="num">37</td><td class="num">58</td><td class="num">95</td></tr>
    <tr><td>D</td><td class="num">0</td><td class="num">95</td><td class="num">95</td></tr>
  </tbody>
</table>
```
:::
:::

## What is a perfect forecast worth? {#evpi}

::: {.two}
::: {}
With a perfect forecast, CellCo picks the best option in each state: C if low, A if medium, A if high.

EV with perfect information = 0.3 × 10 + 0.5 × 80 + 0.2 × 260 = **95**

EVPI = 95 − 56 = **39**, the same number as the smallest EOL.
:::
::: {}
::: {.route-question}
No market study, however good, is worth more than CNY 39 million to this decision. A study that costs more should not be bought.
:::
:::
:::

[In Session 2 we price a real, imperfect survey (EVSI) with a decision tree.]{.note-line}

## Change the probabilities {#emv-explorer data-hold="true"}

```{=html}
<div class="widget" id="ex">
  <div class="w-controls">
    <label class="w-slider">P(low) <strong id="ex-pl">0.30</strong><input type="range" id="ex-l" min="0" max="1" step="0.01" value="0.3"></label>
    <label class="w-slider">P(high) <strong id="ex-ph">0.20</strong><input type="range" id="ex-h" min="0" max="1" step="0.01" value="0.2"></label>
    <span>P(medium) <strong id="ex-pm" style="color:#9a5f10">0.50</strong></span>
  </div>
  <svg id="ex-svg" viewBox="0 0 1160 250" role="img" aria-label="Expected monetary value of each alternative at the chosen probabilities"></svg>
  <div class="w-readout" id="ex-out" aria-live="polite"></div>
</div>
<script>
(function () {
  const root = document.getElementById('ex');
  if (!root) return;
  root.addEventListener('click', (e) => e.stopPropagation());
  const O = [['A', 'New LFP line', [-120, 80, 260], '#0F6E6B'], ['B', 'Sodium-ion retrofit', [-40, 60, 150], '#E29A2D'],
             ['C', 'Tolling contract', [10, 40, 70], '#BE654C'], ['D', 'Do nothing', [0, 0, 0], '#5A91BE']];
  const W = 1160, L = 260, R = 30, x0 = -150, x1 = 300;
  const X = (v) => L + (v - x0) / (x1 - x0) * (W - L - R);
  const sl = document.getElementById('ex-l'), sh = document.getElementById('ex-h');
  function draw(moved) {
    let pl = +sl.value, ph = +sh.value;
    if (pl + ph > 1) { if (moved === 'l') { ph = +(1 - pl).toFixed(2); sh.value = ph; } else { pl = +(1 - ph).toFixed(2); sl.value = pl; } }
    const p = [pl, 1 - pl - ph, ph];
    document.getElementById('ex-pl').textContent = pl.toFixed(2);
    document.getElementById('ex-ph').textContent = ph.toFixed(2);
    document.getElementById('ex-pm').textContent = p[1].toFixed(2);
    const emv = O.map((o) => o[2].reduce((s, v, i) => s + v * p[i], 0));
    let bi = 0; emv.forEach((v, i) => { if (v > emv[bi] + 1e-9) bi = i; });
    const bestState = [0, 1, 2].map((i) => Math.max(...O.map((o) => o[2][i])));
    const evpi = bestState.reduce((s, v, i) => s + v * p[i], 0) - emv[bi];
    let g = '';
    for (const v of [-150, -100, -50, 0, 50, 100, 150, 200, 250, 300]) g += `<line x1="${X(v)}" x2="${X(v)}" y1="8" y2="214" stroke="${v === 0 ? '#333F4A' : '#B9C1C6'}" stroke-width="${v === 0 ? 1.5 : 1}"/><text x="${X(v)}" y="238" text-anchor="middle" font-size="17" fill="#333F4A">${String(v).replace('-', '−')}</text>`;
    O.forEach((o, i) => {
      const y = 14 + i * 50, s = emv[i];
      g += `<text x="${L - 16}" y="${y + 26}" text-anchor="end" font-size="20" font-weight="${i === bi ? 700 : 400}" fill="#1C242B">${o[0]} · ${o[1]}</text>`;
      g += `<rect x="${Math.min(X(0), X(s))}" y="${y + 6}" width="${Math.max(2, Math.abs(X(s) - X(0)))}" height="30" fill="${o[3]}" ${i === bi ? 'stroke="#1C242B" stroke-width="2.5"' : 'opacity=".75"'}/>`;
      g += `<text x="${s >= 0 ? X(s) + 8 : X(s) - 8}" y="${y + 28}" text-anchor="${s >= 0 ? 'start' : 'end'}" font-size="18" fill="#1C242B">${s.toFixed(1).replace('-', '−')}</text>`;
    });
    document.getElementById('ex-svg').innerHTML = g;
    document.getElementById('ex-out').innerHTML = `Highest EMV: <span class="best">${O[bi][0]} · ${O[bi][1]}, ${emv[bi].toFixed(1)}</span> &nbsp; EVPI: <b>${evpi.toFixed(1)}</b> CNY million. Try to find the P(low) at which A stops being the best.`;
  }
  sl.addEventListener('input', () => draw('l'));
  sh.addEventListener('input', () => draw('h'));
  draw('l');
})();
</script>
```

## Activity 2 · Price your own risk {#act2 .activity data-hold="true"}

[On your own · 5 minutes · write before you click]{.act-label}

::: {.prompt}
You are CellCo's CEO. Each gamble is a fair coin toss. Would you accept it for the company? Answer on paper first.
:::

```{=html}
<div class="widget" id="lot">
  <div class="lottery" id="lot-rows"></div>
  <div class="lot-result" id="lot-out" aria-live="polite">Answer all four on paper, then enter your answers here.</div>
</div>
<script>
(function () {
  const root = document.getElementById('lot');
  if (!root) return;
  root.addEventListener('click', (e) => e.stopPropagation());
  const G = [100, 200, 400, 800];
  const ans = G.map(() => null);
  const rows = document.getElementById('lot-rows');
  rows.innerHTML = G.map((x, i) => `<span class="ln">Gamble ${i + 1}</span><span class="lq">Win <b>CNY ${x} million</b> or lose <b>CNY ${x / 2} million</b></span>` +
    `<span class="lbtn"><button type="button" data-i="${i}" data-v="1" aria-pressed="false">Accept</button><button type="button" data-i="${i}" data-v="0" aria-pressed="false">Decline</button></span>`).join('');
  function result() {
    const out = document.getElementById('lot-out');
    if (ans.some((a) => a === null)) { out.textContent = 'Answer all four on paper, then enter your answers here.'; return; }
    const acc = G.filter((x, i) => ans[i]);
    let R, txt;
    if (!acc.length) { R = 60; txt = 'You declined every gamble, so your risk tolerance is below CNY 100 million. Use R = 60.'; }
    else { R = Math.max(...acc); txt = `The largest gamble you accept is win ${R} or lose ${R / 2}, so your risk tolerance is about <b>R = CNY ${R} million</b>.`; }
    const odd = ans.some((a, i) => a && ans.slice(0, i).some((b) => !b));
    out.innerHTML = txt + (odd ? ' You accepted a larger gamble after declining a smaller one: check your answers.' : '') +
      `<br>Keep this R. On the next slides you will see which option it favors.`;
    root.dataset.r = R;
  }
  rows.addEventListener('click', (e) => {
    const btn = e.target.closest('button'); if (!btn) return;
    const i = +btn.dataset.i; ans[i] = btn.dataset.v === '1';
    rows.querySelectorAll(`button[data-i="${i}"]`).forEach((x) => x.setAttribute('aria-pressed', x === btn));
    result();
  });
})();
</script>
```

[Rule of thumb: your risk tolerance R is about the largest X for which you accept "win X or lose X/2" on a coin toss.]{.hint}

[The certainty equivalent (CE) is the sure amount you would accept instead of the gamble. A smaller R bends the curve more, so the low-demand loss of A weighs more than its high-demand gain.]{.note-line}

## Change the risk tolerance {#ce-explorer data-hold="true"}

```{=html}
<div class="widget" id="ce">
  <div class="w-controls">
    <label class="w-slider">Risk tolerance R <strong id="ce-r">100</strong>
      <input type="range" id="ce-in" min="0" max="1000" step="1" value="169" aria-describedby="ce-out">
    </label>
    <span>CNY million, log scale</span>
  </div>
  <svg id="ce-svg" viewBox="0 0 1160 320" role="img" aria-label="Certainty equivalent of each alternative as risk tolerance changes, with the chosen risk tolerance marked"></svg>
  <div class="w-readout" id="ce-out" aria-live="polite"></div>
</div>
<script>
(function () {
  const root = document.getElementById('ce');
  if (!root) return;
  root.addEventListener('click', (e) => e.stopPropagation());
  const P = [0.3, 0.5, 0.2];
  const O = [['A', 'New LFP line', [-120, 80, 260], '#0F6E6B'], ['B', 'Sodium-ion retrofit', [-40, 60, 150], '#E29A2D'],
             ['C', 'Tolling contract', [10, 40, 70], '#BE654C'], ['D', 'Do nothing', [0, 0, 0], '#5A91BE']];
  const ce = (v, R) => -R * Math.log(v.reduce((s, x, i) => s + P[i] * Math.exp(-x / R), 0));
  const rMin = 50, rMax = 3000;
  const fromSlider = (s) => rMin * Math.pow(rMax / rMin, s / 1000);
  const W = 1160, H = 320, L = 70, Rm = 150, T = 14, B = 46, y0 = -80, y1 = 60;
  const X = (r) => L + Math.log(r / rMin) / Math.log(rMax / rMin) * (W - L - Rm);
  const Y = (v) => T + (1 - (v - y0) / (y1 - y0)) * (H - T - B);
  function draw() {
    const r = fromSlider(+document.getElementById('ce-in').value);
    document.getElementById('ce-r').textContent = Math.round(r);
    let g = '';
    for (const v of [-80, -60, -40, -20, 0, 20, 40, 60]) g += `<line x1="${L}" x2="${W - Rm}" y1="${Y(v)}" y2="${Y(v)}" stroke="${v === 0 ? '#333F4A' : '#B9C1C6'}" stroke-width="${v === 0 ? 1.5 : 1}"/><text x="${L - 10}" y="${Y(v) + 6}" text-anchor="end" font-size="17" fill="#333F4A">${String(v).replace('-', '−')}</text>`;
    for (const t of [50, 100, 200, 500, 1000, 2000, 3000]) g += `<text x="${X(t)}" y="${H - 18}" text-anchor="middle" font-size="17" fill="#333F4A">${t}</text>`;
    g += `<text transform="translate(18 ${(T + H - B) / 2}) rotate(-90)" text-anchor="middle" font-size="16" fill="#66727C">certainty equivalent</text>`;
    for (const [s, lab] of [[180, 'C to B, R ≈ 180'], [835, 'B to A, R ≈ 835']]) g += `<line x1="${X(s)}" x2="${X(s)}" y1="${T}" y2="${H - B}" stroke="#66727C" stroke-dasharray="4 5"/><text x="${X(s) + 6}" y="${T + 16}" font-size="15" fill="#66727C">${lab}</text>`;
    const vals = O.map((o) => ce(o[2], r));
    let bi = 0; vals.forEach((v, i) => { if (v > vals[bi] + 1e-9) bi = i; });
    const SHORT = { A: 'A · LFP line', B: 'B · Na-ion', C: 'C · Tolling', D: 'D · Nothing' };
    const ends = O.map((o, i) => [i, Y(ce(o[2], rMax))]).sort((a, b) => a[1] - b[1]);
    for (let k = 1; k < ends.length; k++) if (ends[k][1] - ends[k - 1][1] < 22) ends[k][1] = ends[k - 1][1] + 22;
    const labelY = Object.fromEntries(ends);
    O.forEach((o, i) => {
      let d = '';
      for (let k = 0; k <= 200; k++) { const rr = rMin * Math.pow(rMax / rMin, k / 200); const v = Math.max(y0, Math.min(y1, ce(o[2], rr))); d += (k ? 'L' : 'M') + X(rr).toFixed(1) + ',' + Y(v).toFixed(1); }
      g += `<path d="${d}" fill="none" stroke="${o[3]}" stroke-width="${i === bi ? 4 : 2.5}"/>`;
      g += `<text x="${W - Rm + 8}" y="${labelY[i] + 6}" font-size="17" font-weight="${i === bi ? 700 : 400}" fill="#1C242B">${SHORT[o[0]]}</text>`;
    });
    g += `<line x1="${X(r)}" x2="${X(r)}" y1="${T}" y2="${H - B}" stroke="#1C242B" stroke-width="2"/>`;
    vals.forEach((v, i) => { if (v >= y0 && v <= y1) g += `<circle cx="${X(r)}" cy="${Y(v)}" r="6" fill="${O[i][3]}" stroke="#1C242B" stroke-width="1"/>`; });
    document.getElementById('ce-svg').innerHTML = g;
    document.getElementById('ce-out').innerHTML = `At R = ${Math.round(r)}: ` + O.map((o, i) => `${o[0]} ${vals[i].toFixed(1).replace('-', '−')}`).join(', ') +
      `. Preferred: <span class="best">${O[bi][0]} · ${O[bi][1]}</span>. As R grows large, each CE approaches its EMV.`;
  }
  document.getElementById('ce-in').addEventListener('input', draw);
  draw();
})();
</script>
```

```{=html}
<table class="wide">
  <thead><tr><th>Risk tolerance R, CNY million</th><th class="num">CE of A</th><th class="num">CE of B</th><th class="num">CE of C</th><th>Preferred</th></tr></thead>
  <tbody>
    <tr><td>50</td><td class="num">−61.3</td><td class="num">9.4</td><td class="num">32.7</td><td class="hit">C</td></tr>
    <tr><td>100</td><td class="num">−21.2</td><td class="num">26.6</td><td class="num">34.8</td><td class="hit">C</td></tr>
    <tr><td>200</td><td class="num">13.2</td><td class="num">37.0</td><td class="num">35.9</td><td class="hit">B</td></tr>
    <tr><td>400</td><td class="num">33.9</td><td class="num">42.4</td><td class="num">36.5</td><td class="hit">B</td></tr>
    <tr><td>1,000</td><td class="num">47.1</td><td class="num">45.8</td><td class="num">36.8</td><td class="hit">A</td></tr>
    <tr><td>Risk-neutral (EMV)</td><td class="num">56.0</td><td class="num">48.0</td><td class="num">37.0</td><td class="hit">A</td></tr>

</table>
```

::: {.bridge}
C is preferred below R ≈ 180, B between 180 and 835, and A only above 835. EMV's choice, A, holds only for a board close to risk-neutral.
:::

## What we learned {#debrief}

::: {.takeaways}
::: {.tk}
Without probabilities, the criterion decides: maximin picks C, minimax regret picks B, and maximax picks A from the same table.
:::
::: {.tk}
With probabilities, EMV picks A at CNY 56 million, and EVPI caps the value of any forecast at CNY 39 million.
:::
::: {.tk .key}
Utility puts the board's risk attitude into numbers. CellCo's choice moves from A to B to C as its risk tolerance falls below 835 and then 180 million.
:::
:::
